battle.name: 雲南回變
battle.theater: 昆明城郊與滇南滇西山區
battle.brief: 咸豐六年三月，雲南清官在昆明處決數名回族首領，馬如龍、馬興才與杜文秀遂率回眾起事，戰火由滇南通海蔓延至臨安、大理與滇西騰越，官軍屢攻不下。叛軍以山寨石堡固守，屢圍昆明，並三度進兵緬甸求援。線膛砲隨英軍遠征隊入滇，遠射程壓過叛軍抬砲，改變攻城戰的規則。

kit.name: 線膛砲
kit.history: 線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠。砲兵第一次可以在射程上贏步兵。

countries: 交戰一方是滇回起義軍，清廷檔案稱「滇回」，地方史籍稱「雲南回變」。起義主體是滇中、滇南的回族武裝：通海那氏的團練為核心，聯同石屏、臨安、建水一帶回族首領所聚人馬，另有漢族鄉勇與少數民族武裝附從。咸豐七年（1857）攻陷臨安府城後，叛軍在滇南連成一片據點；咸豐十年（1860）各路首領會盟，推杜文秀為大元帥，檔案亦記作「帥」，全軍改以帥制節制，杜文秀坐鎮臨安、大理、楚雄三處樞紐，馬如龍、馬興才各領一軍，馬如龍主滇南與滇中，馬興才主石屏、瀘西一線。另一方是清廷與地方武力：雲南省文武官員、漢族團練與鄉勇、由回族綠營改編而成的回練，以及同治年間自湖南、貴州入滇的湘軍與黔軍，並有江蘇經長江上游運來的糧餉軍火。咸豐八年（1858）起岑毓英出任雲南巡撫並總攬滇中軍務，其弟岑毓寶領湘軍入滇佐之，江蘇巡撫丁日昌在江南籌辦洋槍洋砲與船運。1865年後太平天國翼王石達開的殘部自黔入滇，岑毓英不得不同時對付兩路敵手，叛軍乘隙向滇東與黔西南伸張。
countriesEn: One belligerent was the Yunnan Muslim insurgent army, recorded in the Qing official files as the Yunnan hui and in the local chronicles as the Yunnan revolt. Its backbone consisted of Hui armed bands in central and southern Yunnan: the militia of the Na clan of Tonghai at the centre, joined by the levies of the Hui leaders of Shiping, Lin'an and Jianshui, together with Han village levies and minority auxiliaries who attached themselves to the cause. After the fall of the prefecture city of Lin'an in 1857, the insurgents held a connected belt of strongholds across southern Yunnan. In 1860 the regional leaders met and raised Du Wenxiu to the rank of grand marshal, the official records also styling him simply the commander-in-chief, and the whole force was reorganised under that single command: Du based himself at the hinge points of Lin'an, Dali and Chuxiong, while Ma Rulong and Ma Xingcai each commanded an army, the former covering southern and central Yunnan, the latter the Shiping and Luxi line. The other side was the Qing court and its local forces: the provincial civil and military officials of Yunnan, Han militia and village levies, the Hui-trained detachments converted from the provincial Green Standard garrisons, and the Xiang and Qian armies that entered Yunnan from Hunan and Guizhou during the Tongzhi reign, supplied with grain and ordnance shipped down the Yangtze by the Jiangsu authorities. From 1858 Cen Yuying served as governor of Yunnan and took overall charge of military operations in the central province, his younger brother Cen Yubao bringing the Xiang army in to support him, while the Jiangsu governor Ding Richang arranged the purchase of Western rifles and guns and their shipment from the south. After 1865 the remnant troops of Shi Dakai, the Taiping Wing King, entered Yunnan from Guizhou, forcing Cen Yuying to fight on two fronts at once and giving the insurgents room to extend towards eastern Yunnan and southwestern Guizhou.
people: 叛軍方面的核心人物是杜文秀。他是生於北京的回族軍人，憑科舉功名出身，長期在滇中活動，兵法嫻熟而書生氣重，屢次在戰敗中收攏散兵重整隊伍，被部下稱為軍師與帥。咸豐十年（1860）被推為大元帥後，他制訂軍令、整肅營伍，以臨安、大理為總部，主持對清軍的長期消耗戰；同治年間他三次派兵入緬求援，又派使團遠赴英國求購軍械，1873年在滇西兵敗身亡，清廷記為戰歿，亦有說法指其自盡。馬如龍、馬興才皆為滇南回族首領，起義初期分據滇南、滇中重鎮，馬如龍其後與清廷議和，重受編制，馬興才則始終抵抗，1860年代後期戰歿滇南。通海那氏一族是叛軍最穩固的地方勢力，壯丁與城鄉據點皆由其掌握。官軍方面，岑毓英自湖南徵集湘軍入滇，歷任雲南巡撫、雲南總督，以官軍大營為堡壘、步步為營，斷糧道而後攻堅，是平叛的主要統帥；其弟岑毓寶統湘軍在滇中、滇南作戰，1869年戰歿滇中。丁日昌管江南軍火與船運，並在1870年代善後雲南教案。叛軍中洪化、劉嶽昭等部先後降清，協助官軍分化回眾。1875年滇西的馬嘉理事件中，一支自八莫入滇的考察隊全隊遇害，成為清廷與英方交涉的焦點。
peopleEn: The central figure on the insurgent side was Du Wenxiu. A Hui military man born in Beijing, he had entered officialdom through the imperial examinations and carried the habits of a scholar into the field: meticulous about drill and paperwork, and credited with gathering scattered soldiers back into order after repeated defeats, his men calling him both strategist and commander. Raised to grand marshal in 1860, he issued the army's orders, tightened its organisation, and made Lin'an and Dali his headquarters, directing a long war of attrition against the Qing. During the Tongzhi years he sent troops into Burma three times to seek help, and despatched an embassy to Britain to buy arms; in 1873 he was defeated in western Yunnan and died, the Qing records stating that he fell in battle while other accounts have him take his own life. Ma Rulong and Ma Xingcai were Hui chiefs of southern Yunnan who held separate strategic zones in the early years of the rising. Ma Rulong later negotiated with the Qing and was reinstated in its service, while Ma Xingcai fought on and was killed in southern Yunnan in the later 1860s. The Na family of Tonghai was the most stable local power in the insurgent camp, controlling both the men and the fortified villages that formed its base. On the Qing side, Cen Yuying recruited the Xiang army from Hunan into Yunnan and served at various times as governor and as governor-general of the province, fighting from entrenched camps and advancing by measured stages, cutting the rebels' supply lines before assaulting their strongholds; he was the main commander in the suppression. His brother Cen Yubao commanded the Xiang troops in central and southern Yunnan and was killed there in 1869. Ding Richang handled the procurement of arms and the shipping arrangements in the lower Yangtze and later dealt with the Yunnan missionary cases of the 1870s. Insurgent commanders such as Hong Hua and Liu Yuechao came over to the Qing and helped divide the Hui ranks. In 1875 the situation in western Yunnan became a diplomatic crisis when a survey party marching in from Bhamo was killed to a man, and the affair drew the Qing court and the British government into direct negotiation.
kits: 卡面這件線膛砲代表的是1850年代歐洲的砲兵技術斷代。線膛讓同樣的藥量走得更遠，砲兵第一次可以在射程上贏步兵：1856年普魯士已用後膛線膛砲攻擊馬格德堡兵工廠，英國的阿姆斯特朗砲與法國的凡賽納砲亦在同一個十年成型，砲口初速與有效射程都遠超舊式滑膛炮。雲南戰場上，線膛砲真正出現已是1860年代末：1868年英軍自緬甸組成的遠征隊隨軍帶有英製線膛野砲，1870年代後上海洋行與江南製造總局、福州船政局又大批售出或仿製阿姆斯特朗式後膛線膛砲與格林快槍，滇軍在岑毓英手上開始成建制裝備來復槍與新式炮兵。在此之前，官軍野戰主要靠過山砲、抬砲等輕型滑膛炮與雲南舊有的紅衣大炮，少量洋砲則是鴉片戰爭前後由廣州、上海輸入的生鐵滑膛炮；回營則靠抬槍、火繩槍、大刀、長矛、竹叉與繳獲的鑄鐵炮，並在城寨上架設自造木砲。糧秣靠挑夫、牛馬與竹筏，沿紅河、金沙江、瀾滄江轉運；滇南滇西的山路、梯田與溜索，決定了雙方都無法快速轉用重炮。
kitsEn: The field gun on the card stands for the artillery break of the 1850s. Rifling let the same charge of powder carry further, and for the first time the artillery could outrange the infantry: the Prussians were already using a rifled breech-loading gun against the Magdeburg arsenal in 1856, while the British Armstrong gun and the French gun of Vincennes were taking shape in the same decade, giving muzzle velocity and effective range well beyond the old smoothbore. In Yunnan the rifled gun really arrived only in the late 1860s. The British column organised from Burma in 1868 marched with British rifled field pieces, and from the 1870s the foreign firms in Shanghai, together with the Jiangnan Arsenal and the Foochow Arsenal, sold and copied Armstrong-pattern rifled breech-loading guns and Gatling guns in quantity; under Cen Yuying the Yunnan army began to be organised around the new small arms and a modern artillery arm. Before that, the government field army relied on light smoothbores such as the mountain gun and the carried gun, together with the old cast-iron Chinese cannon inherited from the Ming; the few Western guns were cast-iron smoothbores imported through Canton and Shanghai around the time of the Opium War. The rebels fielded carried matchlocks and the big broadswords, spears and bamboo tridents of the country people, together with captured cast-iron pieces, and set up improvised wooden guns on their earthworks. Grain and ammunition moved by human carriers, bullocks and pack animals, and by bamboo rafts along the Red, Golden and Mekong rivers; the mountain tracks, terraced fields and ropeways of southern and western Yunnan decided that neither side could shift heavy artillery quickly.
tactics: 叛軍的戰法以地利為先。滇南滇西多山，處處可築石砌堡寨、依梯田關口設卡，壕溝、鹿砦與埋置火藥組成陷坑，攻守兩手都靠短兵與地形。他們慣打圍城打援：兵分兩部，一部逼近城池，另一部伏於山谷岔口，待官軍入山峽再縱兵截擊，湘軍幾次在楚雄、寧遠之間遭此伏擊。攻城時用雲梯、藤排、挖地道與埋藥包破牆，兵眾以大刀開路，衝鋒前先用冷兵器與火藥齊射官軍陣腳；守城則以砲位壓制坡下的官軍，消耗其糧秣。官軍一方以湘軍的結營制為骨：扎營先挖壕、環築土壘，列槍陣與刀盾陣層層拒馬，步步為營，先斷叛軍糧道、再攻其城寨，岑毓英屢次以取回通海、建水、石屏的糧源為先手，斷糧三日，叛軍即潰。1869年後線膛砲與格林快槍開始隨軍使用，砲兵在遠程壓制城頭與砲位，為步軍在城牆下清出缺口，攻城戰的節奏因此改變。
tacticsEn: The insurgents put terrain first. Southern and western Yunnan is a country of mountains, and stone-built stockades, passes sealed with terraced fields, ditches, palisades and buried charges made the basis of every position, both attack and defence resting on short weapons and on the ground itself. Their preferred pattern was to invest a city and destroy its relief column: the force was split, one part pressing the walls while the other lay in wait at the mountain forks, and the Xiang troops were cut up in the gorges between Chuxiong and Ningyuan more than once. At the walls they used scaling ladders, vine mantlets, saps and powder charges to breach the ramparts, crowds of men with broadswords driving ahead of the assault after a shower of cold weapons and loose powder had broken the government line; from the defences their guns covered the government ranks on the slope and wore down their supplies. On the government side the spine of the campaign was the Xiang habit of entrenching: on arriving, the camp was dug in and ringed with earthwork, ranks of pike and of shield and blade stood behind the chevaux-de-frise, and the advance was made stage by stage, first cutting the rebels' grain route and then assaulting the stockades. Cen Yuying repeatedly made the recapture of Tonghai, Jianshui and Shiping his first priority, on the reasoning that three days without grain broke a rebel army. After 1869 rifled guns and Gatling guns came into use with the army, and the artillery could engage the ramparts and the rebel gun positions from long range, clearing a breach at the foot of the wall for the infantry, and so changing the rhythm of siege.
data: 戰役時長與範圍：起於咸豐六年（1856），主戰役至光緒元年前後落幕，滇南最後堡寨到1876年才被攻破，逃入緬甸的殘部又在當地抗爭至1890年代，前後牽動二十餘年。疆域方面，叛軍一度控制滇南、滇西與滇中大部，昆明數度被圍。兵力方面，清廷與地方文牘常寫叛軍數十萬，更可信的推估是數萬量級：1860年代包圍昆明時，攻城一線可辨的兵力約一二萬；岑毓英麾下的湘軍、黔軍與滇軍團練合計亦在數萬，所需糧餉多自貴州、湖廣沿江轉運。距離上，昆明至騰越官道約七百公里，騰越至八莫再行約二百公里，1869年叛軍三路入緬即循此線；1871年赴倫敦的使團自雲南經仰光、加爾各答至英倫，行程逾一萬公里、歷時近一年。1875年馬嘉理事件發生於八莫附近，護衛規模只有數十人。1870年代上海方面售予清廷的格林快槍數以千計，線膛野砲數十門，江南製造總局自1870年起仿製阿姆斯特朗式砲。
dataEn: On duration and extent: the rising began in 1856, the main campaigns ended around the first year of the Guangxu reign, the last stronghold in southern Yunnan did not fall until 1876, and the refugees who pushed into Burma carried on resisting there into the 1890s, so that the whole affair ran for more than twenty years. In territory the insurgents at one point held most of southern, western and central Yunnan, and Kunming was besieged more than once. On numbers, Qing despatches and local accounts habitually speak of hundreds of thousands of rebels, while a more defensible estimate puts the field force in the tens of thousands: the force that besieged Kunming in the 1860s can be identified as somewhere around ten to twenty thousand, and the Xiang, Qian and Yunnan militia under Cen Yuying together also numbered in the tens of thousands, with most of their grain coming from Guizhou and Huguang down the river. On distance, the official road from Kunming to Tengyueh runs about seven hundred kilometres and the road from Tengyueh to Bhamo a further two hundred; the 1869 incursion into Burma followed that line in three columns, and the 1871 embassy to London travelled from Yunnan via Rangoon and Calcutta to Britain, over ten thousand kilometres and close to a year on the way. The Margary affair of 1875 happened near Bhamo with an escort of only a few dozen men. During the 1870s the foreign firms in Shanghai sold the Qing court several thousand Gatling guns and some dozens of rifled field pieces, and the Jiangnan Arsenal began copying Armstrong-pattern guns in 1870.
cause: 雲南回變的起因並非單一事件，而是長年的族群衝突被一次屠殺點燃。滇中、滇南回漢雜居，爭水、爭田、爭集市、由地界與墳地引發的糾紛時有發生；地方官府多偏袒漢族士紳，回族被逐出城鎮貿易、廟地與墳場，團練與綠營又以鎮壓之名屢加抄掠。回族中有識之士在太平天國前期的戰亂中看到團練與土司武力不可恃，遂整頓教門、囤糧練兵，通海那氏、石屏馬氏正是此中最有組織者。導火線是咸豐六年二月末至三月，清廷在昆明將數名回族首領連同親眷處決，其中一人是馬如龍的族人，消息傳回滇南滇西，馬如龍、馬興才即率眾起事，杜文秀隨即在滇中響應，戰事由清廷的一次處決擴為全省戰爭。往後三年，戰事牽連滇中、滇南、滇西，並與太平軍入滇的時機重疊，使原有矛盾與新添的兵禍互相放大。
causeEn: The outbreak of the Yunnan revolt was not the work of a single incident but the accumulation of long-standing friction between communities, lit by one massacre. Hui and Han lived together in mixed villages in central and southern Yunnan, and disputes over water, land, market rights, boundary strips and burial grounds arose constantly; the local authorities generally favoured the Han gentry, the Hui were excluded from trade in the towns and from mosque and burial ground, and the militia and the Green Standard detachments repeatedly raided them in the name of pacification. Some of the more literate Hui, watching the collapse of the militia and the tusi levies during the early years of the Taiping war, concluded that armed organisation was the only security and began to regularise their religious communities, to store grain and to drill; the Na clan of Tonghai and the Ma family of Shiping were the most systematic in this. The spark was the execution, in the last weeks of the second month and the third month of 1856, of a number of Hui leaders together with their families in Kunming, one of them a kinsman of Ma Rulong. The news carried back to southern and western Yunnan, Ma Rulong and Ma Xingcai rose with their men, Du Wenxiu answered the call in central Yunnan, and what had begun as a single execution by the Qing court turned into a province-wide war. Over the following three years the fighting spread through central, southern and western Yunnan, overlapped with the arrival of the Taiping armies, and let the older quarrels and the newer horrors of war feed on one another.
impact: 雲南回變改變的不只是雲南。它迫使清廷正視雲南的邊防與軍制問題：岑毓英在滇首建以線膛砲、格林快槍、來復槍裝備的新式炮兵與洋槍隊，湘軍系的將領自此長期主政雲南，雲南成為晚清最先規模化引進西洋火器的省分之一，江南製造總局與福州船政局仿製的線膛砲，日後也在中法戰爭與西南邊防中使用。戰爭癱瘓了滇南、滇西的茶、銅、鹽與馬幫貿易，商路斷絕數年，許多府縣田地拋荒，恢復不易。外交上，叛軍西向緬甸求援與清廷的閉關政策相撞，1875年馬嘉理事件、1876年雲南教案相繼發生，中英於煙台條約後開放雲南通商，1885年中法續議條約與1886年北京條約更開蒙自、騰越為商埠，法國於是取得進入雲南的實際通道，中法戰爭隨即把戰火推到滇南邊境。英國亦藉平叛之機拓展緬甸影響，1890年代劃界把中緬邊線北推，回流邊地的雲南回族餘部成為邊疆治理的長期難題。
impactEn: The Yunnan revolt changed more than Yunnan. It forced the Qing court to take the province's frontier and military systems seriously: under Cen Yuying the province built the first new-style artillery and musket units in the empire equipped with rifled guns, Gatling guns and Peabody rifles, and the Xiang officers who had fought in Yunnan went on to govern the province for years afterwards. Yunnan became one of the first provinces to introduce Western firepower on a large scale, and the Armstrong-pattern rifled guns copied at the Jiangnan and Foochow arsenials later saw service in the Sino-French war and on the southwestern frontier. The war paralysed the tea, copper, salt and mule-train trade of southern and western Yunnan; the caravan routes were cut for years, land in many prefectures and counties was abandoned, and recovery was slow. In diplomacy, the rebels' westward appeal to Burma collided with the Qing policy of exclusion: the Margary affair of 1875 and the missionary cases in Yunnan in 1876 followed one another, Britain obtained the opening of trade in Yunnan after the Chefoo convention, the 1885 Sino-French convention and the 1886 Peking convention opened Mengzi and Tengyueh as treaty ports, and France obtained a real road into the province, so that the Sino-French war pushed the fighting to the southern frontier. Britain used the pacification to extend its Burmese influence, and the boundary demarcations of the 1890s pushed the Sino-Burmese line north, leaving the Yunnan Muslim remnants who had fled over the border as a permanent problem of frontier governance.
result: 光緒元年（1873）杜文秀在滇西兵敗身亡，叛軍失去唯一能號令全局的樞紐，隨後兩年節節潰敗：光緒二年（1876）滇南彌勒牛鼻一帶的最後堡寨被官軍攻破，殘部退入緬甸，在那裡繼續抵抗英緬當局至1890年代之後。清廷以很大代價收回滇南、滇西，恢復府縣建置，但雲南地方武力化、團練化的格局已經成形，湘系將領治滇的局面延續到清末，為二十世紀初雲南地方軍閥政治埋下伏線。戰後的雲南並未因此安定：通商口岸開放、教案頻仍、外國使節與商隊不斷深入，1880年代雲南同時面對法國自越南北進的壓力與英國自緬甸西來的探測，清廷被迫在改土歸流與整軍備禦之間尋找出路，而雲南回變留下的一整套城寨防禦經驗、土司與團練的武裝網絡，以及線膛砲與洋槍在本地的手腕，都成為後來雲南防務與軍事現代化討論的基礎。
resultEn: In 1873 Du Wenxiu was defeated and killed in western Yunnan, and with his death the insurgents lost the only pivot that could hold the whole rising together; they collapsed over the next two years, the last stockade in the Niu Bi area of Mile in southern Yunnan falling to the government army in 1876, while the survivors who crossed into Burma kept resisting the Burmese and British authorities there into and beyond the 1890s. The Qing recovered southern and western Yunnan at heavy cost and restored the prefectures and counties, but the pattern by which the province's armed life ran on local levies and militia had already been set, and the practice of Hunan officers governing Yunnan ran on into the late Qing, laying groundwork for the warlord politics of early twentieth-century Yunnan. The province was not settled by this: the opening of the treaty ports, the succession of missionary cases, the steady penetration of the province by foreign envoys and caravans, and in the 1880s the pressure of France advancing from northern Vietnam and the British probes from Burma, all left the Qing searching for a way forward between administrative reform and the reorganisation of the province's defence. The stockade warfare of the revolt, the armed network of tusi and militia that it left behind, and the local handling of rifled guns and Western muskets all became the raw material of later argument over Yunnan's defence and military modernisation.
